title: Benny Goodman's offers
summary: Goodman asked him to join to match Miff Mole; he declined without a higher offer.

story.theme_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the leader and his bands
story.community_name: Working for Benny Goodman: the perfectionist bandleader

blocks.x: You just told me something about Benny Goodman that we didn't know before. Tell me again.
Well, I was in New York, laying off there, and Benny Goodman was at the Astor Hotel, and his trombone player was Miff Mole at that time; he was using only one trombone.

So I came to listen to him, because I would always see Benny Goodman when I could -- he was the best in clarinet, a good musician. So I went over to the Astor one night and I got my little table there, and I listened to him for awhile, and for some reason or another, he found out that I was there, and he came by my table -- and he asked me, he said, "I would like to have you in the band so you can match with Miff Mole." So I said, "Well, that would be fine, but I don't know if I could leave Duke Ellington right now."

Well, that was that, and one time when I was in Boston and he happened to be in Boston, too, at the I think it was the Metropolitan Theatre or something, and I saw him. And still, he said, "I would like to have you", and I said something about how much could he offer me because I was making a pretty good salary with Duke Ellington. But I don't know how much I told him, but whatever I told him, he said, "Well, what do you want me to do? Buy you a home?" I said,
"No, I don't want you to buy me a home, but if you want me, you have to pay for me."
Do you remember what period of time it was in New York when he asked you? Was it in the forties or the thirties?
I guess so -- it was around there.
Maybe sometime before you left for Harry James.
